(p-393) In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surat al-Fath (The Victory)

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have given you a clear victory﴾.

The verified view held by the majority is that the victory meant here is the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyah, because it was a great victory.

The clarification of this is that the aforementioned treaty was the means by which the Muslims were able to mix with the disbelievers, call them to Islam and explain to them its excellences, so that many of the tribes of the Arabs entered Islam because of it.

What further clarifies this is that those who witnessed the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyah with the Prophet ﷺ in Dhu al-Qa'dah of the sixth year were one thousand four hundred.

When the Prophet ﷺ intended to campaign against Makkah, after the disbelievers broke the covenant, his departure toward Makkah was in Ramadan of the eighth year.

With him were ten thousand fighters. This shows that the aforementioned treaty is among the greatest of conquests, since it was the cause of the strength of the Muslims and the increase of their numbers.

The victory mentioned is not the conquest of Makkah, although a group of scholars said so.

We say this because most scholars hold the view we have stated, and because the apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates it, since this Surah of al-Fath was revealed after the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyah, on his ﷺ journey back to Madinah.

The past tense in His saying ﴿Indeed, We have given﴾ indicates that this victory has already occurred. The claim that it is the conquest of Makkah, which did not happen until about two years after that, contradicts the apparent meaning.

The verse concerning the conquest of Makkah indicates the future, not the past, and it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When the help of God and the victory come﴾ [an-Nasr: 1].

We have clarified in our book "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab" the meaning of the lam in His saying (p-394) ﴿that God may forgive you your earlier and later sins﴾ [al-Fath: 2].

The author said in "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab":

(p-396) In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surat al-Fath

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have given you a clear victory﴾ ﴿that God may forgive you﴾.

It is not hidden what comes to mind of the contradiction between this cause and its effect, since God's granting victory to His Prophet does not appear to be a cause of His forgiving him.

The answer to this is in two respects:

The first, which is the choice of Ibn Jarir for the evidence of the Book and the Sunnah upon it: the meaning is that God's granting victory to His Prophet indicates, by implication (dalalat al-iltizam), the Prophet's thanks for the blessing of victory. God forgives him what preceded and what followed because of his thanking Him with various kinds of worship for that blessing. So the Prophet's gratitude is necessarily connected to the blessing of victory, and forgiveness is consequent upon that necessary matter.

As for the evidence of the Book for this, it is in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When the help of God and the victory come﴾ ﴿and you see people entering the religion of God in multitudes﴾ ﴿then glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness; indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance﴾ [an-Nasr: 1-3].

In this noble Surah He explicitly states that his glorifying his Lord with His praise and seeking forgiveness from Him, in thanks for the blessing of victory, is a cause for the forgiveness of his sins, since He ordered his glorifying with praise and his seeking forgiveness with the fa' (then) after the coming of victory and help, in the manner of an effect following its cause. Then He clarified that this thanks is the cause of forgiveness by His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance﴾.

As for the evidence of the Sunnah, it is in his ﷺ saying, when some of his companions said to him, "Do not exhaust yourself in works, for God has forgiven you what preceded of your sin and what followed": "Shall I not be a grateful servant?"

So he ﷺ made clear that his striving in works to thank for that blessing, and the consequence of forgiveness upon striving in works, is beyond doubt.

(p-397) The second respect: that His saying "Indeed, We have given" implies, by implication (dalalat al-iltizam), jihad in the way of God, because it is the greatest means of victory, and jihad is a cause of the forgiveness of sins. The meaning would then be: that God may forgive you by means of your jihad, which is understood from the mention of victory. And God knows best.

The words of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿That they may increase in faith along with their faith﴾.

What this noble verse indicates, that faith increases, is also indicated by other verses of the Book of Allah,

- such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when His verses are recited to them, it increases them in faith﴾ [al-Anfal: 2],

- and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice﴾ [al-Tawbah: 124],

- and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That those who were given the Scripture may be certain, and those who believed may increase in faith﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 31],

along with other verses. We have explained this repeatedly.

The truth beyond doubt is that faith increases and decreases, as the Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah (the People of the Sunnah and the Community) hold, and revelation (al-Wahy) from the Book and the Sunnah has indicated this, as has already been mentioned.

* *

The words of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿And to Allah belong the armies of the heavens and the earth﴾.

In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentions that He has the armies of the heavens and the earth. In al-Muddaththir He made clear that none knows these armies except Him, in His saying: ﴿And none knows the armies of your Lord except Him﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 31].

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 48, verse 5:

﴿That He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein eternally, and remove from them their misdeeds. And that is, in the sight of Allah, a great triumph.﴾ ﴿And that He may punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the polytheist men and polytheist women who assume about Allah an assumption of evil.﴾

The most apparent and most sound of the opinions regarding this verse is that the lam in His saying ﴿li-yudkhila﴾ ("that He may admit") is connected to His saying: ﴿He it is who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers that they might increase in faith along with their faith﴾ [al-Fath: 4].

The clarification of the meaning: ﴿He it is who sent down tranquility﴾, that is, calm and assurance in the truth, into the hearts of the believers, so that they might thereby increase in faith, in order that He might admit them, through their assurance in the truth and their increase in faith, ﴿into gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾.

The implicit meaning by contrary inference (mafhum al-mukhalafa, i.e., the understanding that the opposite of what is stated is implied) in His saying ﴿in the hearts of the believers﴾ is that the hearts of non-believers are not like this. This is so, and therefore their recompense differs from the recompense of the believers, as Allah, exalted is He, has explicitly stated in His saying: ﴿And that He may punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the polytheist men and polytheist women who assume about Allah an assumption of evil.﴾

The clarification of the meaning is that He, exalted is He, granted success to the believers by sending down tranquility and increasing their faith, and He left the others, from among the polytheists and hypocrites, in wretchedness, so He did not grant them success in this, in order that He might recompense each according to the requirement of his deeds.

This verse is similar in meaning to His saying, exalted is He, at the end of surah al-Ahzab: ﴿And the human being bore it. Indeed, he was a wrongdoer and ignorant, that Allah may punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the polytheist men and polytheist women, and that Allah may accept the repentance of the believing men and believing women﴾ [al-Ahzab: 73].

(p-395)

The Exalted and Majestic said, in this noble verse, that He recompenses the polytheist men and women and the hypocrite men and women with three punishments: His wrath, His curse, and the Fire of Hell.

﴿And Allah became angry with them, and cursed them, and prepared for them Hell, and evil is it as a destination.﴾

In some other verses He also clarified some of the consequences of these three things:

• As for His wrath, He says: ﴿And whoever has My wrath descend upon him has indeed fallen﴾ [Ta-Ha: 81],

• and as for the curse, He says: ﴿And whoever Allah curses, you will not find for him any helper﴾ [An-Nisa: 52],

• and as for the Fire of Hell, He says: ﴿Our Lord, indeed whomever You admit to the Fire You have indeed disgraced﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 192].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 48, verse 8:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾.

In this noble verse, He - majestic and exalted - made clear that He sent His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ as a witness, a bringer of good tidings, and a warner.

He - exalted be He - has also made clear that He will raise him ﷺ on the Day of Resurrection as a witness over his ummah, and that he is a bringer of good tidings to the believers and a warner to the disbelievers. He - exalted be He - said concerning his ﷺ testimony over his ummah on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness and bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness over these people?﴾ [An-Nisa: 41], and His saying: ﴿And [mention] the Day when We will raise up in every nation a witness against them from themselves, and We will bring you as a witness against these [people]﴾ [An-Nahl: 89].

The verse of An-Nisa and the verse of An-Nahl, which are mentioned and which indicate his ﷺ testimony over his ummah on the Day of Resurrection, explain this verse of Al-Fath.

As for what we mentioned, that he is a bringer of good tidings to the believers and a warner to the disbelievers, it is clarified in His saying: ﴿So We have only made it easy in your tongue that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous and warn thereby a hostile people﴾ [Maryam: 97].

We have already explained this at the beginning of Surat al-Kahf. What He - majestic and exalted - mentioned in this noble verse, He mentioned it with additional detail in Surat al-Ahzab, in His saying: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner, and as one who invites to Allah by His permission and as a light-giving lamp﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 45-46].

His saying here: ﴿Indeed, We have sent you as a witness﴾ is a delayed (muqaddarah) circumstantial clause (hal). His saying: ﴿and a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾ - both of them are circumstantial clauses (hal) conjoined (ma'tuf) to a circumstantial clause.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 48, verse 11:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Then who could prevent anything from Allah for you if He intended harm for you or intended benefit for you?"﴾.

Allah, glorified and exalted, commanded His Prophet to say to the hypocrites who stayed behind from him and offered false excuses: ﴿Then who could prevent anything from Allah for you if He intended harm for you or intended benefit for you?﴾ [al-Fath: 11]. That is, no one can repel the harm that Allah intends to send upon you, nor withhold the benefit that He intends to bestow upon you. There is no one who benefits except Him, and no one who harms except Him, exalted is He. No one is able to repel harm that He has willed or to withhold benefit that He has willed.

What this noble verse contains is clarified in other verses of the Book of Allah, such as His saying in al-Ahzab: ﴿Say, "Who is it that can protect you from Allah if He intends for you harm or intends for you mercy?" And they will not find for themselves besides Allah any ally or any helper.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 17].

And His saying at the end of Yunus: ﴿And if Allah should touch you with adversity, none can remove it except Him; and if He intends for you good, there is no repeller of His bounty﴾, to the end of the verse [Yunus: 107].

And His saying in al-An'am: ﴿And if Allah should touch you with adversity, none can remove it except Him; and if He should touch you with good, then He is over all things competent﴾ [al-An'am: 17].

And His saying in al-Ma'idah: ﴿Say, "Then who could prevent anything from Allah if He intended to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, and his mother and everyone on earth entirely?"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 17].

And His saying in Fatir: ﴿Whatever Allah grants to the people of mercy, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, none can release it after Him﴾, to the end of the verse [Fatir: 2].

And His saying in al-Mulk: ﴿Say, "Have you considered: if Allah should destroy me and those with me, or have mercy upon us, who will protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?"﴾ [al-Mulk: 28].

(p-397) We have already mentioned some of the verses indicating this at the beginning of Surah Fatir, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Whatever Allah grants to the people of mercy﴾, to the end of the verse [Fatir: 2]. And in Surah al-Ahqaf, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Say, "If I have invented it, then you cannot prevail for me against Allah in anything"﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 8].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 48, verse 26:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers﴾.

In this noble verse, He - majestic and exalted - mentioned that He sent down tranquility (al-sakinah) upon His Messenger and upon the believers. Al-sakinah includes reassurance (al-tuma'ninah), calm settling upon the truth (al-sukun ila al-haqq), steadfastness (al-thabat), and courage in the face of severity (al-ba's).

He - majestic and exalted - also mentioned His sending down tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers in Surah Bara'ah (al-Tawbah), in His saying: ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers﴾ [al-Tawbah: 26]. He mentioned the sending down of His tranquility upon His Messenger in His saying in Bara'ah: ﴿When he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed, Allah is with us." So Allah sent down His tranquility upon him﴾ [al-Tawbah: 40], and so on.

He mentioned His sending down tranquility upon the believers in His saying: ﴿He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them﴾ [al-Fath: 18], and so on.

None of these verses specified the place where the tranquility is sent down. In this noble surah, however, He has made clear that the place of the sending down of tranquility is the hearts, in His saying: ﴿It is He who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers﴾ [al-Fath: 4], and so on.

**The Qur'anic verse:** ﴿He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion.﴾

What Allah, exalted is He, mentioned in this noble verse, He mentioned in Surat At-Tawbah and Surat As-Saff, and in those two places He added that He is the one who does this, even if the polytheists dislike it. So He said in both places: ﴿He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, even if the polytheists dislike it.﴾ [At-Tawbah: 33], [61 - 9].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 48, verse 29:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves﴾.

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah al-Ma'idah, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah will bring forth a people whom He loves and who love Him, humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 54].

(p-398) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And their likeness in the Gospel is that of a seed which sends out its shoot and strengthens it, so it grows firm and stands upon its stalk, pleasing the sowers﴾.

Ibn Kathir, Ibn Dhakwan and Ibn Amir read this word "shat'ahu" with a fatha on the ta'. The rest of the Seven read it with a sukun on the ta'.

Most of the Seven, except Ibn Dhakwan, read ﴿fa-azarahu﴾ with an alif after the hamza.

Ibn Dhakwan, on the authority of Amir, read "fa-azarahu" without an alif after the hamza, in its bare form.

Most of the Seven, except Qunbul, read ﴿ala suqihi﴾ with a silent waw after the sin.

Qunbul, on the authority of Ibn Kathir, read it with a silent hamza in place of the waw. And on his authority, the hamza is vowelled with a damma after the sin, followed by a silent waw.

This noble verse shows that Allah has set forth in the Gospel a likeness of the Prophet ﷺ and his companions: that they are like a seed which first appears thin, weak and scattered; then some of it grows around the rest, thickens, and matures until it becomes strong and firm, and its excellence pleases those who farm and know it. Likewise, the Prophet ﷺ and his companions were, at the beginning of Islam, few and weak; then they continued to increase and grow in strength until they attained what they attained.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿like a seed which sends out its shoot﴾ means its offshoots, so it grows on its sides. His saying ﴿fa-azarahu﴾, according to the reading of the majority, is from al-muwazarah (mutual support), meaning assistance and strengthening. Some scholars said: ﴿fa-azarahu﴾ means it made it equal to it in height. Both meanings have been given as the explanation of the verse of Imru' al-Qays:

"In a bow-field, where the wild sand-willow (al-Sal) has matched its plants, / Driving the armies of the spoilers and disappointing them."

As for the reading of Ibn Dhakwan, ﴿fa-azarahu﴾ without an alif, the meaning is "shadda azrahu," i.e., strengthened it.

From this is His saying, may He be exalted, concerning Musa: ﴿And appoint for me a minister from my family, Harun, my brother. Strengthen my back through him﴾ [Ta-Ha: 29-31], the verse.

His saying ﴿fa-istaghlaza﴾ means that the crop became thick after having been thin. His saying ﴿fa-istawa﴾ means it became complete and matured ﴿upon its stalk﴾, i.e., upon its stem.

(p-399) What this noble verse contains of the likeness mentioned in the Gospel, struck for the Prophet ﷺ and his companions, that at the beginning of their affair they would be few and weak, and after that they would multiply and grow strong, has been clarified in verses of the Book of Allah, may He be exalted, such as His saying: ﴿And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land, fearing that people would snatch you away, and He sheltered you and strengthened you with His help﴾ [al-Anfal: 26].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah had already helped you at Badr when you were humiliated﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 123], and His saying: ﴿Today those who disbelieved have despaired of your religion, so do not fear them but fear Me﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 3], and other verses besides these.
